Biblical Worldview
BIB-lih-kul WURLD-vyoo
noun
From English biblical (of or pertaining to the Bible) + calque of German Weltanschauung (world-view, world-outlook), coined by Kant and developed by Hegel and Dilthey. The compound became standard in evangelical and Reformed apologetics through Abraham Kuyper's Lectures on Calvinism (1898) and Francis Schaeffer's apologetics.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

A biblical worldview is the comprehensive framework of beliefs, values, and interpretive commitments derived from Scripture through which a believer understands all of reality—God, creation, humanity, history, ethics, and destiny. It is the alternative to every humanistic, materialistic, or spiritually pluralistic framework, and it begins with the fear of the Lord as the beginning of wisdom (Prov. 1:7). A genuine biblical worldview is not a set of policies or political positions but a set of first principles: that God is Creator and Sovereign over all things; that man is fallen and incapable of autonomous redemptive wisdom; that Scripture is the final, authoritative norm for faith and practice; that Christ is Lord over all domains—church, family, state, culture, vocation; and that history moves toward a definite eschatological end in which God vindicates His name. Paul commands the renewal of the mind (Rom. 12:2) that constitutes the cognitive dimension of sanctification, and he warns against being taken “captive through hollow and deceptive philosophy” (Col. 2:8). The weapons of this intellectual warfare are “every thought to make it obedient to Christ” (2 Cor. 10:5). Abraham Kuyper's famous declaration—“There is not a square inch in the whole domain of our human existence over which Christ, who is Sovereign over all, does not cry: 'Mine!'”—captures the scope. A biblical worldview is not merely a checklist for cultural commentary; it is the mind shaped by the Word, seeing all things through the lens of creation, fall, redemption, and consummation.

Origin & Era

Biblical worldview: the comprehensive interpretive framework derived from Scripture that shapes a believer's understanding of all reality, including creation, human nature, ethics, history, and ultimate purpose; the Christian alternative to secular or pluralistic world-pictures.

expand to see more

BIB'LI-CAL WORLD'VIEW, noun. (Modern coinage.) A comprehensive, Scripture-governed framework for interpreting all of reality; the cognitive and moral structuring of experience according to the categories and commitments of Holy Scripture.

Distinguished from a “Christian worldview” in popular use: a biblical worldview insists that Scripture, not Christian tradition alone, is the authoritative source for the framework's first principles.

Rooted in Abraham Kuyper's neo-Calvinist concept of Weltanschauung: Christianity is not merely a religion among others but a comprehensive life-system governing every domain of human thought and activity.

Francis Schaeffer popularized the term in evangelical apologetics, emphasizing that every person operates from a worldview and that the biblical worldview stands or falls on the truth of its foundational presuppositions.

Presuppositional apologists (Van Til, Bahnsen) argue that a biblical worldview is not merely one option among many but the necessary precondition for any coherent knowledge, ethics, or science.

Key Scripture

Proverbs 1:7 — "The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge, but fools despise wisdom and instruction."

Romans 12:2 — "Do not conform to the pattern of this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind. Then you will be able to test and approve what God's will is—his good, pleasing and perfect will."

Colossians 2:8 — "See to it that no one takes you captive through hollow and deceptive philosophy, which depends on human tradition and the elemental spiritual forces of this world rather than on Christ."

2 Corinthians 10:5 — "We demolish arguments and every pretension that sets itself up against the knowledge of God, and we take captive every thought to make it obedient to Christ."

Modern Corruption

The term biblical worldview has been domesticated into a political brand or culture-war checklist, stripped of its theological depth and used to baptize preferred policy positions rather than to describe a comprehensive, Scripture-formed mind.

expand to see more

The corruption of biblical worldview language is subtle precisely because the language sounds maximally Christian. The problem is that “biblical worldview” in popular usage has become a shorthand for conservative political positions, a way of saying “our side” rather than describing a disciplined, Scripture-governed interpretive framework. When a political candidate claims to govern from a “biblical worldview” while demonstrating no knowledge of Scripture's teaching on mercy, the poor, or the sanctity of human life in all its dimensions, the phrase has become hollow. Similarly, worldview curricula that function as culture-war apologetics rather than integrative biblical theology train students in combativeness without the wisdom that genuine worldview thinking requires.

The recovery is the Kuyperian original: every square inch belongs to Christ, and that means the hard, patient, long-term work of bringing every discipline—economics, literature, science, law, art—under the lordship of Christ as revealed in Scripture, not merely defending political positions. A biblical worldview begins with humility (Prov. 1:7) before it reaches cultural application. The renewing of the mind (Rom. 12:2) is a lifelong work of sanctification, not a catechism completed in a semester. True worldview education produces citizens who think Christianly about everything, not partisans who know which side to be on.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

German Weltanschauung (Kant, Hegel) transplanted into Christian apologetics by Kuyper and Schaeffer names the comprehensive character of the Christian mind that Scripture demands.

expand to see more

German Welt — world; the totality of created reality over which Christ is Lord and Scripture speaks

German Anschauung — view, outlook, perception; the interpretive framework that organizes all experience

Dutch levens- en wereldbeschouwing — life-and-worldview; Kuyper's full phrase, emphasizing that Christianity is a comprehensive life-system, not a private religion

Greek nous — mind; Paul's term for the cognitive faculty renewed by the Spirit (Rom. 12:2), the faculty that a biblical worldview exercises

Latin presuppositio — prior assumption; the presuppositional apologist's term for the foundational commitments that determine all subsequent reasoning

Usage

"A biblical worldview is demonstrated not by knowing which political party to support but by applying Scripture's categories (creation, fall, redemption, consummation) to every domain of thought and life."

"Kuyper's sphere sovereignty doctrine provides the structural logic of a biblical worldview: each sphere of society (church, family, state, school, market) has its own God-given authority structure, and biblical thinking respects those distinctions."

"Pastors who preach only personal and ecclesial applications of Scripture, never addressing the church's engagement with culture, business, law, and learning, are training congregants in a partial rather than a biblical worldview."
